correctness.rationale: Two-cycle equations reduce exactly to s=A sin(s)cos(d), d=B cos(s)sin(d); |A|<1 forces s=0. The positive roots are entirely in positive sine lobes, each classified using the strict decrease of d cot(d). On p=0, equal Jacobians along the antipodal orbit have characteristic polynomial lambda(lambda²+g cos(d)lambda-a cos(d)), so elementary quadratic Schur inequalities give an exact and complete sink interval per lobe. For k>=1 the fold and loss-of-attraction boundaries are the unique monotone roots stated in the result. Expanding at the sine maximum gives fold Bk=m-1/(2m)+O(m^-3) and exit Rk=m+4/m+O_A(m^-2), hence width 9/(2m)+O_A(m^-2). Standalone symbolic Jacobian/identity checker and finite numeric diagnostics passed; infinite validity derives from the written proof.
